texts.text: Say the {ore} vein on {street} drops just under halfway. If I prune it then, do we get any calc off it?

replies.text: Nothing. Only what's above the middle counts.
replies.response: Right. Leave it to climb, then. Writing that down.

replies.text: Prune it hard, see what comes off.
replies.response: Will do. James said under halfway gives you nothing, but he says a lot of things.

replies.text: Prune it light. Little and often.
replies.response: Little and often. Got it. I think.

texts.text: The {ore} vein on {street} is sitting a couple over the target you gave me. Do I prune it back?

replies.text: Leave it. A few either side is fine.
replies.response: Leaving it. Feels wrong standing there doing nothing, but fine.

replies.text: Yes. Right back to the number.
replies.response: Did it. Got about nothing off it, and a look from James.
Up? It's already over. I'll do it if you say, but I'm confused.

texts.text: Two veins off target today. The {ore} one on {street} is a bit high, the other one's miles low. I've only got time for one.

replies.response: Miles low, then. Thought so. Going now.

replies.text: The high one. Get the calc in.
replies.response: Fair enough. The low one's still sinking, mind.
Okay. They'll both be worse tomorrow, though, won't they.

texts.text: If I leave the {ore} vein on {street} alone for a few days, does it drift back to the middle on its own?

replies.text: No. It keeps going whichever way it's leaning.
replies.response: So a low one just gets lower. That's grim. Right.
James laughed when I told him. I don't think he meant it nicely.
Is that real? I'll write it down with a question mark next to it.

texts.text: Is a hard prune just two light ones done at once?

replies.text: No. Hard cuts deeper and pays a bit better per point.
replies.response: Better per point. So hard when there's plenty above halfway. Got it.
Okay. James just wrote 'no' on a post-it and stuck it to my arm.

texts.text: The {ore} vein on {street} is right at the top and won't go any higher. James says if it sits there long enough it spreads. Is he winding me up?

replies.text: He's not. Leave it at the top a few days and it seeds a new one nearby.
replies.response: A new one. From nothing. I might need to sit down.

replies.text: He is. It just sits there.
replies.response: He said you'd say that. He said to tell you you're wrong, and to use those words.

texts.text: The {ore} vein on {street} has gone right down to nothing. Is it dead?

replies.text: Not yet. Cultivate it today and it can come back.
replies.response: On it now. Didn't sleep much, if I'm honest.
Okay. Feels like leaving a dog tied up outside a shop, but okay.
There's nothing left to prune. I checked twice.

texts.text: Two veins, same growth. One's on good ground, one's on rubbish ground. Same calc off a prune?

replies.response: So it's the ground, not me. Weirdly a relief.
That's what I thought. Then why does one always come up short. I measured.

texts.text: Bloke at the bus stop asked what I do. I said gardening. He asked what I grow. I panicked and said rocks.

replies.response: He moved seats.
Noted. I'll just nod. Nodding's safe.

texts.text: Archie said we need to paint the gate on the vein at {street}, and I should get some striped paint from B&Q. The guy said they're all out of striped paint. Do you think plain white would be ok?

replies.response: Good. I'll tell Archie they were out. He said they usually are.
Right. He also sent me for a long weight last week. I stood there forty minutes.

texts.text: My mum asked what the new job is. I said agriculture. She's told the whole family I'm a farmer now.

replies.response: She's bought me wellies.
What is the truth, though. Genuinely asking.

texts.text: James ate his lunch standing up again. Should I get him a chair or is that rude.

replies.response: Leaving it. He's got three chairs. He knows.
Did. He put his coat on it.

texts.text: It's raining on {street}. Do veins mind rain? I've put my coat over the {ore} one just in case.

replies.response: Getting my coat back, then. It's quite wet.
Thought so. I'm freezing, though.

texts.text: Got paid. Put half in savings. First time I've had savings. Doesn't feel like anything. It's just a number that's bigger.

replies.response: Bit disappointing, then. Still keeping it.
Got a meal deal with the posh crisps. Felt like a king for about ten minutes.

texts.text: There was a man on {street} watching me all morning. Didn't say anything. Had a lanyard. Should I be worried?

replies.text: Tell me if he comes back.
replies.response: Will do. He wrote something down when I left.
That's what I thought. Council don't usually take photos, though.

texts.text: Archie gave me a fish. Not a cooked one. Said a bloke owed him. What do I do with a fish.

replies.response: I haven't got an oven. I've got a kettle.
He says he doesn't do returns.

texts.text: Pop quiz. Same calc, two buyers. One's round the corner. One's in a nicer postcode, pays more, bus fare's a fiver. Where we going?

replies.response: Good. Fiver on the bus, more than that back. Same calc, posher street.

replies.text: Round the corner. Saves the fare.
replies.response: Saves a fiver, loses twenty. You'd make a terrible accountant.
Quick's nice. Paid's nicer.

texts.text: Say you've got sixty of something and the price is good today. Shift the lot?

replies.response: There it is. Dump the lot and you're the reason it's cheap tomorrow.

replies.text: All of it, while it's good.
replies.response: Then it's not good any more, is it. You did that.

replies.text: Sit on the lot till it's better.
replies.response: Might be. Rent don't take might.

texts.text: James knocked out two batches of pearls. One's better than the other. Same price for both?

replies.response: Course. Don't tell James I asked. He'll want a raise.
Simple's how you end up giving the good ones away. No.

texts.text: Tip for nothing. Never tell a buyer it's your last one. They'll want to know why, then they'll want a discount.

replies.text: You told me it was your last one.
replies.response: Yeah. And look what it got me. You.
Noted, he says. Write it down.

texts.text: Bloke outside the station flogging umbrellas at a tenner. Pound shop's two doors down. It's chucking it down. He's cleaning up.

replies.response: Right product, right street, right weather. That's the whole job, that.
That's retail. Robbery's when you don't hand over the umbrella.

texts.text: Found a tenner in my coat. Pretty sure it's yours from the chippy. Sending it over.

replies.response: No. Don't like owing. Sent.
Don't make it a thing.

texts.text: Sneezed six times walking past a clock shop in Clerkenwell. Six. Not going down there again.

replies.response: Don't.
It's not hay fever. It's time. Antihistamines don't know what to do with it.

texts.text: Buyer turned up with a pigeon on his shoulder. He didn't mention it. I didn't mention it. Deal went fine.

replies.response: That's the job. Pigeon looked like it was the one doing the haggling, mind.
Didn't ask. You don't ask.

texts.text: My nan's asked if I've got a proper job yet. Told her logistics. Now she wants a business card.

replies.response: Already ordered. Says 'Consultant'. She's framed it.
She's eighty-four and on the parish council. No.

texts.text: You've been grafting. Don't make it weird. Chips are on me Friday.

replies.response: Yeah, well. Don't be late.
Know I don't. That's what makes it chips and not wages.

texts.text: James rang at six this morning to say my invoice had a typo. It was a receipt. For chips.

replies.response: There was. That's the annoying bit.
Can't. He'll ring at seven about the second one.

texts.text: Went past the {ore} one on {street}. Someone's chained a bike to the fence. Leave a note or take the wheels?

replies.response: Left a note. Took one wheel. Meet in the middle.
Harmless now. Next week it's a bike rack and a queue.

texts.text: Homework question. Papers are 90p, rent's £400 a week. How many papers a day to cover it? It's for the homework.

replies.response: That's what I got. I was hoping one of us was wrong.
It isn't. I checked. Twice.
I do sell crisps. That's not what the homework asked.

texts.text: Rep wants me to stock a new crisp. Prawn cocktail and lime. I said I'd think about it. Do I have to actually think about it?

replies.response: Oh, good. I'd been thinking about it.
I didn't promise. I said it. Is that the same? Now I'm thinking about that.

texts.text: A woman's bought the same lottery numbers off me every Saturday for nine years. Today she changed one. I don't know who to tell.

replies.response: I can't ask her why. It's her business. I'll just worry.
I have. Sorry. Thank you. I feel a bit better.

texts.text: Two men in suits bought chewing gum and talked about a lock-up by the canal like I wasn't there. People do that. I'm the till.

replies.response: Something about Thursdays and not enough men. I wrote it on a crisp box. Sending a photo.
I am out of it. I'm the till.

texts.text: Man from the Guild came in for a paper and complained about his suppliers for ten minutes. I nodded. I know a lot about his suppliers now.

replies.response: Two of them are the same man with different invoices. That's all. Sorry it's not more.
I'm not. The till's exactly my size.

texts.text: Someone from the Conclave takes The Times and a magazine about clocks. Paid for the year up front. Cash. Exact change.

replies.response: I shouldn't tell you. It's on the label. I'm sending you the label.
Probably. I still counted it twice.

texts.text: Found my uncle's notebook for the yard. Same thing every day: 'Watered. Spoke to it.' He never wrote down what he said.

replies.response: Probably. I tried hello. Felt stupid. Did it again the next day.
I'm not asking the vein. It's never liked me.

texts.text: Kettle's on if you're passing. No reason. I've just got too many teabags.

replies.response: Okay. I'll get the good biscuits out. Not the very good ones.
That's fine. They don't go off. Well, they do. Not soon.

texts.text: Card machine's down. Put up a sign saying CASH ONLY SORRY. Then felt bad and added another sorry.

replies.response: Three. Someone added one. I don't know who.
Is it? Lost two sales. Both very understanding about it.

texts.text: Delivery came with forty copies of a fishing magazine I didn't order. Nobody on Whitechapel Road fishes. I've sold six.

replies.response: The same man, six times. I've stopped asking.
I tried. They said keep them. That's never good.

texts.text: Lip's fine now. Before you ask. Nadia's asked four times.

replies.response: Thank you. Don't tell Des it's fine. He'll stop bringing soup.
Also fine. Mostly. Thank you for asking properly.

texts.text: Swept the yard. There's nothing in it now. Swept it anyway.

replies.response: He'd say I missed a bit. I did miss a bit.

replies.text: Want me to look at it?
replies.response: No. It's all right. It's just a yard now. That's allowed.

texts.text: Question. What decides the quality of a pearl? Think before you answer. It will be a novel experience.

replies.response: Correct. Patience, not luck. Write it down somewhere you'll see it.
The calc is the calc. You are the variable. You are usually the variable.
In the sense that fast makes it worse, yes. I assume that isn't what you meant.

texts.text: Which of Plato's dialogues mentions orichalchum? I am measuring how much you retain.

replies.response: Retained. I'm almost moved. Almost.
The Republic is about justice. You would know that if you had read the Republic.
That isn't Plato. That isn't even the right century.

texts.text: In Atlantis, orichalchum was the second most precious metal. Name the first.

replies.response: Gold. Unimaginative of them, but accurate.
Silver came after both. Plato was quite clear. Unlike you.
Loyalty to the product. Touching. Also wrong.

texts.text: Enhancement powder. Which calc goes in? This is the easy one. I chose it deliberately.

replies.response: Good. I had a speech prepared. I'll keep it for next time.
Time goes in pearls. You have made pearls. With your hands. In front of me.
No. There is a label on the jar. I wrote it myself, in capitals.

texts.text: A woman on the bus told me my cardigan was 'brave'. I have worn it for thirty-one years. Nobody has ever called it brave.

replies.response: It is wool. Wool cannot be brave. I am keeping it.
Thank you. She was also eating an egg on a bus, so I don't know why I listened.

texts.text: An optician offered to straighten my glasses today. Free of charge. I left.

replies.response: I can see perfectly well through them. And she said 'bless' when she saw the arm.
Thank you. Nobody ever says fair enough. They say 'James'.

texts.text: A client wrote 'oricalcum' in an email. Twice. I have charged him extra.

replies.response: It's my business. Pedantry is a line item.
Yes. I thought you might understand. I told Archie. He asked what pedantry was.

texts.text: I made one pearl more than the order needed. Within tolerance. Barely. It's with your things, provided you don't say thank you.

replies.response: There it is. Couldn't help yourself.
Good. That's the correct response.

texts.text: Sending you a letter to a client. Tell me if it's rude. It's meant to be. I need to know it isn't rude enough to lose him.

replies.response: Just is the target. Twenty pounds for your time. Don't spend it on anything I'd see.
Then I've overdone it. I'll remove a semicolon.

texts.text: Archie hugged me. In public. A football result. I would like it noted that I did not consent.

replies.response: Thank you. I have also noted it.
I patted him. On the shoulder. Twice. Don't tell him I counted.

texts.text: Owen brought me a tea without being asked. Correct milk. I never told him. I'm unsettled.

replies.response: He is. That's why I took him on. I didn't expect it to be used against me.
I drank the tea. That isn't the point.

texts.text: Couldn't sleep, so I reread the Critias. It stops mid-sentence. Plato simply stopped. Two and a half thousand years and nobody has finished it.

replies.response: Don't be absurd. I've drafted four pages.
It isn't. He got bored, or he died. Neither is a point.

texts.text: I've found three lists of who holds time calc. None agree. One includes a man who's been dead six years. He was reliable, to be fair.

replies.text: Want me to check the names?
replies.response: Yes. Start with anyone still drawing breath. I'll send the pages.
The newest one has him on it twice.

texts.text: Des left a flask of tea and a sandwich on my desk. He says I missed lunch. He's right. Don't tell him I said that.

replies.response: Already have. He put the good mustard in it.
I did. He asked whether I'd had breakfast. One problem at a time.

texts.text: A buyer offered to pay early if I left the quantity off the invoice. I told him I could leave his name off it as well.

replies.response: It's written. He can sign it or shop elsewhere.
an invoice without a number is just an argument waiting to happen

texts.text: The shared cupboard has six keys. Four open it. Nobody knows what the other two open. I'm collecting them before someone calls this a system.

replies.response: Good. Bring string. The labels have gone missing.
Not until I know what they open.

texts.text: One Time Pearl left over from a cancelled order. It's yours if you'll collect it. I've written it down, before you ask.

replies.response: At the shop. Ask for me.

replies.text: Give it to someone who needs it.
replies.response: I will. I'll put your name against the gift.

texts.text: Woman at the shop asked if I'd retired. I was carrying two crates. I told her I'd consider it after the third.

replies.text: Need a hand with the third?
replies.response: Yes. Come by at four. Don't look pleased with yourself.
She held the door. That's something.

texts.text: I rang three people for ten units of time calc. All three said they had it. Turns out it was the same ten units changing hands. I've cancelled two trips.

replies.response: That's the question. I know where it started, don't know who has it now
Yes. One call each. Write down who actually has the jar.

texts.text: Rain got through the shop roof again. Stock's dry. The accounts book isn't. I've hung it up by the till like a warning.

replies.response: Bring a folder too. Next leak gets filed properly.
He can. Whether he will is a different question.
